messages.body_plain:
That is expected. HTML widgets are not only about the HTML output, but
more importantly, the dependencies that they carry. For example,
Leaflet requires leaflet.js/leaflet.css/... The rmarkdown and shiny
packages are smart enough to figure out these dependencies and insert
them into the HTML head. For WordPress, authors normally don't have
write access to the HTML head at the time of publishing a blog post.
If you are the site admin, you can probably change your template files
to include these dependencies in the head.

Other options include: 1) publish these widgets separately to
RPubs.com or ShinyApps.io; 2) use R Markdown v2 to write blog posts
instead of WordPress.

Regards,
Yihui

In the case of V8/JavaScript, there is no need to do so, because it is
easy to know which part is source code and which is output in R. (See
what I wrote in the Github issue) In the case of Julia, the source
code and output are mixed on the Julia side, and I will have to split
them after I receive everything back from Julia.

I've realized that after running spin() the *.Rmd is produced but then deleted
and replaced by the corresponding *.md and *.html. I would like
to actually keep the *.Rmd to edit it sometimes. Have tried
spin("CBBiot_PCA_rcharts_log.R",precious=FALSE,format="Rmd")

but even in that case I get
output file: CBBiot_PCA_rcharts_log.md

What should I do to keep the *.Rmd file?
Thanks
Agus
